result.title: Measuring What Matters: A Causal Reliance Score for Histopathology Image Segmentation
result.comment: 15 pages, 8 figures, accepted into Medical Image Understanding and Analysis (MIUA) 2026 conference
result.summary: Reliable histopathology segmentation requires models that rely on pathology-relevant structures rather than spurious background correlations. In this work, we argue that improving architectures alone is insufficient if models continue to rely on spurious correlations rather than pathology-relevant features. We introduce a causality-inspired evaluation framework based on controlled interventions that explicitly probes model sensitivity to foreground tissue structure and background/domain variation. Building on this, we propose the Causal Reliance Score (CRS), a metric that quantifies the relative sensitivity of model predictions to foreground perturbation versus background/domain variation under controlled interventions. To support this analysis, we design augmentation strategies that act as implicit counterfactual interventions during training, encouraging invariance to nuisance factors while preserving morphology. We demonstrate how these interventions reveal behavioural differences between models that are not captured by standard metrics such as Dice or IoU. While we instantiate our framework using a self-supervised transformer (CAUSE-ViT), the primary contribution of this work is not a new architecture, but a principled intervention-based methodology and evaluation metric for auditing model behaviour in medical image segmentation. Our results suggest that evaluating model behaviour through counterfactual interventions is essential for developing reliable and clinically robust medical image segmentation systems.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出因果启发式评测框架：通过对前景组织与背景／域变化的受控干预，给出 Causal Reliance Score，量化分割模型对病理相关结构与伪相关背景的相对敏感度，并用训练期增广作为隐式反事实干预，以 CAUSE-ViT 为例展示 Dice／IoU 未反映的行为差异。
